{"content":"## How a Python extension can affect the runtime mode

CPython 3.13 introduced experimental free threading, a configuration that can run with the global interpreter lock (GIL) disabled. A Python extension must explicitly declare that it supports this mode. If an extension is imported without that declaration, CPython warns and enables the GIL.

Declaring support is separate from making the extension’s code thread-safe. The declaration mechanism also differs depending on whether an extension uses multi-phase or single-phase initialization.

On Windows, the compiler does not automatically receive the `Py_GIL_DISABLED` macro when building extensions. The active configuration can be checked through `sysconfig`."}
